evidence_quotes: Tobelo, Indonesia led all hotspots with 19 recorded events, followed by Mohr, Iran (15) and Nikolski, Alaska (13)
February 3rd and February 14th each saw 9 events in a single day, the highest daily counts recorded
Tobelo, Indonesia warrants close monitoring. With 19 events in 31 days — including a M5.7 on Feb 14 — this region is showing elevated, sustained activity
Mohr, Iran's shallow quakes pose a local hazard. Several events struck at depths under 10 km (including a M4.9 at just 8.5 km)
Data Caveat: This report is based on synthetic USGS-variant data... and should not be used for official hazard assessments or emergency planning purposes
criticisms: No explicit 24-hour actions are recommended — the report never tells a coordinator to 'alert county X', 'request a USGS briefing on Tobelo', 'verify shelter capacity near Mohr', or 'notify Alaska tsunami warning center'. The risk watch section describes conditions but stops short of prescribing actions.

The data caveat explicitly states the report 'should not be used for official hazard assessments or emergency planning purposes', which directly undermines any operational utility and would cause a coordinator to discard the report entirely.

Prioritization is present but implicit — the three watch items are listed as equal-weight bullets with the same warning symbol; no explicit 'highest priority' or tiered ranking is given to help triage resource allocation.
Monitoring priorities name regions but lack specific magnitude thresholds or time windows to trigger escalation (e.g., 'if another M5.5+ occurs in Tobelo within 7 days, escalate to...').
No geographic specificity for response staging — which Indonesian province, which Alaskan communities, which Iranian districts should be contacted or pre-positioned for?
